messages.text: Three days had passed since my transfer, and I had settled into something resembling a routine. Wake up at six. Catch the 7:15 train. Arrive at school by 7:45. Sit through classes that I understood maybe half of. Eat lunch with Anna, Mei, and Kenji — a group that had somehow adopted me without any formal discussion. And then, after school, I would find myself in the library.

The library was an old building, constructed decades ago when the school had first been founded. The wooden floors creaked in specific places — I had already memorized which boards to avoid. The shelves towered overhead like ancient guardians, their spines forming a mosaic of faded colors and peeling labels. The air smelled of paper and dust and something else, something older that I could not identify.

messages.name: Kazuhiko
messages.text: "You're popular," I said, not really meaning to say it out loud.

We reached the cafeteria, and she led me to a table near the window where two other students were already seated. One of them was the meticulous note-taker from the front row. The other was a boy I had not noticed before, with glasses and an easy smile.

messages.name: Anna
messages.text: "Mei, Kenji — this is Kazuhiko. Kazuhiko, this is Mei and Kenji."
The introductions were brisk, efficient. Mei looked up from her notebook, her eyes meeting mine with that same unsettling recognition I had felt earlier.
She returned her attention to her notebook without elaborating, her pen resuming its relentless dance across the page. Kenji offered me a sympathetic shrug.

messages.name: Kenji
messages.text: "Don't mind her. She's always like that. Sit down, new guy. The curry rice here is terrible, but the miso soup is surprisingly decent."

I sat down, my mind still spinning from Mei's cryptic remark. The afternoon passed in a blur. By the final bell, I had learned that Anna was in the photography club, Kenji was obsessed with a mobile game, and Mei had a habit of making cryptic statements. As I walked toward the school gate, the setting sun painted the sky in shades of orange and pink. I felt a strange mixture of exhaustion and anticipation.

That evening, I decided to take a walk along the riverbank near my new apartment. The water was calm, reflecting the dim lights of the city. I thought about how invisible I had felt at my old school, but here, somehow, I was being noticed. It was both unnerving and exciting.

messages.name: Kenji
messages.text: "Hey, Kazuhiko! Wait up!" I turned to see Kenji jogging toward me, waving his phone. "I was just at the bank — I mean the ATM — and guess what? My account is suddenly overflowing. Like, weird amount of money. You didn't happen to... do anything, did you?"

I stared at him, bewildered. What was he talking about? But before I could answer, my phone buzzed with a message from an unknown number: "Welcome to Seishin Academy. Your orientation period has ended. Report to the library after school tomorrow. We'll explain everything." The question that had been nagging me grew louder: What exactly had I transferred into?
